caption:
Elon Musk is telling people to send Grok Bot a photo of their credit card and let it shop for them.
He says SpaceX "will make you whole" if the agent makes a purchase mistake or leaks a card.
The company's terms still say it is not responsible for what the agent does.

Would you hand your credit card to an AI agent?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: The Next Web, Teslarati · Photo: Business Insider

slides.headline: Musk says send Grok a photo of your credit card. If it messes up, *SpaceX pays*

slides.heading: Shopping with a *card photo*
paras: Musk told X users they can take a picture of their credit card, drop it in the chat, and let Grok Bot find the best deal and order the item.
On October 15, a user said Grok Bot booked them a flight from a photo of their card. Musk replied: "This works well."

slides.heading: "We will *make you whole*"
paras: Musk added that if Grok Bot makes a purchase mistake or leaks your card, SpaceX "will make you whole." He noted that this has "never happened yet."
He did not say what the pledge covers or how anyone would claim it.

slides.heading: The *fine print*
paras: The company's terms say it is "not responsible for User Content or Agentic Actions" and generally cap its liability at the greater of fees paid or $100.

paras.t: For now, the pledge is a post on X, not a published policy.

slides.heading: Amazon *shut the door*
paras: Users say Amazon now blocks Grok Bot from placing orders. Musk replied that there are "far more purchasing websites than just Amazon."
Then he went further: "Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon."

slides.hook: AI agents now spend real money for real people. Follow to see who pays when they get it wrong.
